findings.title: User verification skipped when Integration row doesn't exist yet
findings.body: The authenticated-user check only runs when an Integration row already exists for the installation_id. If the installation webhook hasn't arrived yet, `Integration.DoesNotExist` makes the view call `pipeline.next_step()` without any user check. An attacker can supply someone else's installation_id before the webhook lands and take over the installation. The same applies to any installation that has no Integration row.

findings.title: KeyError if integration metadata lacks sender
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes the webhook stored a sender. Integrations created through `build_integration` without a sender in state, and older records, have no such key. Those cases raise a KeyError and produce a 500 instead of the error page. Use `.get()` and treat a missing sender as an explicit failure.

findings.title: redirect_uri not URL-encoded in authorize URL
findings.body: The authorize URL is built with an f-string, so `redirect_uri` (and the other parameters) are not URL-encoded. A redirect URI containing `?`, `&` or `:` can be misparsed by GitHub. Build the query string with `urlencode`.

findings.title: Token exchange and get_user_info errors not handled
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` is called outside the try block, so a network error raises unhandled. `get_user_info` can also raise on an invalid token or an API error. Either failure surfaces as a 500 instead of the intended error page.
